exposure: cardiac comorbidities (congestive heart failure, arrhythmia, valvular disease, pulmonary disorders, history of thromboembolism)
cohort: The study included 51,841 delivery hospitalizations to women aged 15-54 years with maternal congenital heart disease, identified from a total of 73,109,790 delivery hospitalizations in the 2000-2018 National Inpatient Sample.
finding: Maternal congenital heart disease (CHD) is becoming more common among US deliveries and is associated with significantly increased risks for severe maternal morbidity, cardiac severe maternal morbidity, placental abruption, preterm delivery, and transfusion.
